units.t: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions and Decimals
Number and the Laws of Arithmetic

unit.title: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages
unit.blurb: Fractions of shapes and amounts, fractions as division, percentages as parts of 100, and comparing fractions, decimals and percentages.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand that a fraction can be a part of a whole or a division, and find unit and non-unit fractions of amounts.

O2.t: Understand percentages as parts of 100 and recognise percentages, decimals and fractions with the same value.

O3.t: Recognise equivalent fractions and compare and order fractions and decimals.

p: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. In **3/5**, the whole is split into **5** equal parts (the denominator) and we have **3** of them (the numerator).
A shape split into 4 unequal pieces is not split into quarters.

p: **Equivalent fractions** have the same value: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8. Multiply (or divide) the numerator and denominator by the same number.
To compare fractions, give them the same denominator: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 2/3 < 3/4.
1/6 is smaller than 1/4: sixths are smaller pieces than quarters.
